question.text: What is the maximum percentage of IPO proceeds that can be allocated towards General Corporate Purposes (GCP)?

explanation.text: The Logic: For IPOs, the amount earmarked for General Corporate Purposes (GCP) must not exceed 25% of the amount being raised. Separately, GCP plus unidentified acquisitions or investments together cannot exceed 35% of the amount raised. The Trap: 35% is the combined cap for GCP plus unidentified acquisitions or investments — not the standalone GCP-only cap. Candidates who remember only the higher number may select this incorrectly. Note: The 25% standalone cap and the 35% combined cap are two distinct limits that apply simultaneously to the objects of the issue.
